# Independent audit: nonaffine reflection plateau and endpoint contraction

Source: `candidate 02c6510b145c2710`.

**Result: PASS.** The author applied the sole requested scope clarification:
d>=1 is now explicit in the general ordinary-depth statement. This avoids
an undefined ordinary nonzero-normal halfspace family in R^0. The planar
application has d=2. No other repair is needed.

## 1. Exact global formula, including every ambient halfspace

A missed point (-1,x) in a through-(0,g) closed ambient halfspace maps
under (-1,x)->(1,2g-x) to a strictly captured point. Reflection preserves
volume and the assumed containment puts that image in B. Together with
the already captured A points, this charges the entire volume |A| to the
two endpoints. Captured boundary points are retained in A; strict missed
points form its exact complement. Pure integer normals also obey the
same reflection argument. The middle contribution is at least m_K, since
g is an ordinary maximizing point. Containing halfspaces may be shrunk
parallel through the source, so the lower bound covers all of them.

Conversely, an arbitrary nonzero-continuous-normal cap of K through or
containing y extends by a sufficiently large negative integer tilt to
capture all of A and exclude all of B. Compactness makes the tilt finite.
The middle trace stays unchanged, giving depth(0,y)<=D_K(y)+|A| after
taking the infimum. Each endpoint similarly admits finite isolation of
any own ordinary cap, while every ambient containing cap retains at
least its own ordinary depth. The exact global maximum is therefore
max{m_A,m_B,m_K+|A|}, with an actual middle realizing point g. No special
orientation, expectation, or centroid rounding enters this formula.

## 2. Actual nonaffine plateau

For the canonical triangle, support values of -aT at each facet normal
are 2a. Thus 2h-aT subset bT is exactly h in (b/2-a)T. Midpoint
compatibility is exactly -h in [c-(a+b)/2]T. Nonnegative coefficients
and their singleton convention at zero are correctly stated. These
inclusions make the convex hull's three integer fibers exact; the
integer endpoints are exposed, and equal endpoint weights at base zero
produce only points already inside the middle fiber.

The ordinary triangle maxima are 2r^2 and their centroids are actual
maximizing points. Hence the displayed global formula follows from the
first theorem. Strict support slack lets h vary in a full neighborhood
while all fiber areas and the exact global depth stay fixed.

For b=c=1, h=(1/10,0), and 0<a<1/4, both inclusions have the claimed
strict margins. The middle depth 2+(9/2)a^2 exceeds both endpoint maxima.
The normalized value differs from 2/9 by a strictly positive numerator
(7/2)a^2 over the common positive mass denominator, and tends to 2/9
as a tends to zero. Each individual body remains positive-dimensional
and strictly compatible. The centroid graph is nonaffine because its
endpoint centroids are zero and its middle centroid is nonzero. Thus
this is an exact globally optimized translation plateau, not a cap-menu
artifact. It refutes only unconditional STRICT translation descent,
not any proposed non-strict inequality.

## 3. Exact contraction and source switch

For p in A and 0<t<=1, convexity gives A_t=p+t(A-p) subset A. Both
midpoint compatibility and reflected containment persist. The three
fibers in their convex hull remain exact and full-dimensional. Ordinary
depth and volume scale by t^d, giving the stated three-entry raw maximum.
Its t^d m_A entry is strictly dominated by m_K+t^d|A| because m_A<=|A|
and m_K>0. Thus the normalized maximum is exactly

    max{m_B,m_K+x}/(k+b+x),  x=t^d|A|.

On the middle-active branch its derivative in x is
(k+b-m_K)/(k+b+x)^2>0; on the endpoint-active branch it is
-m_B/(k+b+x)^2<0. Therefore decreasing x gives strict descent only up
to the actual possible source switch, and reverses its sign afterwards.
The note explicitly retains this limitation. In the concrete plateau
family m_K=m_B=2, every positive x is middle-active and contraction
about zero keeps the centroid defect h unchanged while descending to
the sharp limiting value. No positive-fiber assertion is made at t=0.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
